name: MarkItDown
description: Document parsing via Microsoft's MIT-licensed MarkItDown library — the default `document.parse` backend, and the one that works on a machine where the user installed nothing on purpose. `pip install 'markitdown[all]'` is a pure-Python install of a few tens of megabytes: no ONNX runtime, no layout-detection model download, no GPU, and no `brew`/`apt` packages to chase. It covers the formats people actually attach — PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX/XLS, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, EPUB, Outlook .msg, Jupyter notebooks, and ZIP archives expanded member-by-member — and it emits markdown natively rather than a flat text dump, so headings stay headings and spreadsheet tables stay tables. The tradeoffs are honest ones: no OCR (a scanned PDF comes back empty and the job says so), no legacy binary `.doc`/`.ppt`, and no element-level structure for a consumer that wants to chunk on document structure. Parses run as jobs: submit returns 202 + a job_id, the caller polls.
tagline: Pure-pip document parsing, no native toolchain
